transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-30 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Mira Patel (Redwood SE), Ravi Narayan (Redwood SE), Erin Wallace (BlueHarbor Head of ML), Tom Reyes (Cloud Infra), Lisa Moreno (FinOps), Jamal Ortiz (Security)

Auto-summary (auto): quick console clinic focused on per-route chargeback, tagging, and how the console maps tokens to teams. Customer wants predictable bills and a plan to do internal showback/chargeback. Action: send playbook, run short baseline, confirm tags, schedule pilot canary for Dedicated.

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. we'll do a 45 minute walkthrough then leave 10 for q and next steps—sound good?
00:06 Erin: yeah that's great, thanks. we wanted practical stuff today, like where do we get the numbers for chargeback and how accurate are they, like at the team level.
00:14 Mira: perfect. quick context: we'll show the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and the billing export. we'll also show the chargeback playbook — it's the same artifacts we use with FinOps teams.
00:23 Lisa: awesome. i'm mostly interested in how we map service names to routes and if we can use our existing billing tags.
00:31 Alex: great to hear. quick housekeeping: we'll share the deck afterwards (link: https://redwood.example.com/decks/chargeback-playbook.pdf) and a sample CSV of the route-level billing export.
00:37 Tom: quick Q — if we want to run this on Dedicated vs Hosted what are the differences for reporting? does Hosted give us per-route visibility?
00:44 Mira: yes Hosted has route-level metrics by default; Dedicated adds reserved capacity and predictable per-hour spend which helps allocation. the console shows normalized per-token cost across both, but Dedicated also exposes pool-level amortized infra cost and utilization.
00:58 Ravi: i'll jump in with a screenshot — heading to the Console now.
01:04 [screen share starts — slight audio lag]
01:12 Mira: ok top-left is 'Usage Overview' — you can slice by time range, team, route, model. see those little badges? those are routes.
01:21 Erin: i see a route called 'payments-v2' — is route the same as service or can one service have multiple routes?
01:26 Mira: routes are logical identifiers you define in the SDK/SDK integration. a single service can certainly push multiple routes — e.g., payments-v1, payments-v2, payments-batch. we recommend mapping routes to billing tags for FinOps.
01:38 Lisa: how do you handle retries and system-initiated tokens? they can skew cost.
01:44 Mira: good call — we have heuristics to filter internal retries and system tokens in the default export. there's a 'customer_token' flag; you can exclude system calls. accuracy isn't 100% — we see occasional transcription oddities, but it's high enough for showback.
01:58 Jamal: security question — does the export contain any PII or full prompts?
02:03 Alex: short answer: no. exports are token-level aggregates and route identifiers, not full prompt bodies. for Private deployments we can suppress more metadata; we also integrate with KMS for key management.
02:15 Tom: can we tie routes to our existing AWS tags? we have team and costcenter tags.
02:20 Mira: yes, you can forward tags in the request metadata; we also ingest a mapping file so Console can translate 'team=payments' to the route automatically. we'll show the mapping tab.
02:31 [clicks]
02:35 Mira: here is the 'Route Mapping' tab. you can upload a CSV that maps tag keys to routes, or use the API to push mapping. once mapped, the per-route dashboard will attribute token counts and cost to those tags.
02:45 Lisa: are the costs shown raw GPU hours or a normalized per-token cost? which should we use for chargeback?
02:53 Mira: Console shows both. the default is an amortized per-token cost that includes GPU, memory, and licensing when applicable. you can also switch to 'infrastructure-only' view which shows GPU-hour allocation and the pool amortization. for chargeback we recommend per-token normalized cost plus an allocation of reserved capacity if Dedicated.
03:12 Erin: in our environment we have bursty traffic — how would the console handle peak vs off-peak billing?
03:18 Ravi: we have 'capacity amortization' settings — you can choose to smooth reserved capacity across billing cycle or attribute spikes to routes active during peak windows. both patterns are supported; the console visualizes the difference.
03:31 Lisa: hmm, for internal chargeback we'd prefer smoothing monthly so teams don't get killed by a big spike.
03:36 Mira: totally reasonable. that's the default for monthly reserved pools. if you want per-event attribution we can show 'actual' mode instead.
03:44 Erin: are there known accuracy limits? you said heuristics for system tokens — any margin of error we should plan for?
03:50 Mira: yes, empirically we see +- 2-5% variance for high-volume routes, worse for very low volume routes due to sampling and rounding. we can run a synthetic baseline to quantify for your traffic profile.
04:05 Tom: about Private deployment — we may need it for compliance. would the console be identical?
04:10 Alex: the control plane behavior is the same; the Private package sends metrics to your control plane in VPC. audit logs and retention policies are configurable. there's some extra work for initial setup but visibility is equivalent.
04:21 Jamal: we require SOC2 plus quarterly attestation — do you have docs to share?
04:24 Alex: yes we'll share our compliance pack. it's in the same folder as the playbook (note: security-deck link shared).
04:31 [Customer asks for an example export]
04:34 Mira: opening 'Billing exports' tab. this is a sample CSV: columns include timestamp, route_id, team_tag, token_count, input_tokens, output_tokens, model, normalized_token_cost, infra_cost, reserved_alloc, region.
04:48 Lisa: can we inject cost adjustments — like we want to add 10% overhead for platform ops?
04:54 Mira: yes you can add markup at the tenant or route level; the console supports multipliers and manual adjustments that show up in the export. we also have 'internal ledger' to store adjustments.
05:05 Erin: wanna see how this maps to our finance tool — we use AcctFlow. can you export to S3 or push via webhook?
05:12 Ravi: both — exports can be pushed to your S3 bucket on a schedule and you can also configure webhooks for realtime row-level events.
05:22 Tom: what about attribution for multi-tenant requests where one request triggers multiple back-end calls?
05:28 Mira: in complex flows we recommend routing each downstream call with its own route and then using a parent-child mapping to roll up costs. Console supports rollups and weighted allocations. there is a little manual work to define the weights, but it's manageable.
05:44 Lisa: ok wild question — can we do per-feature chargeback? like feature flag X uses model Y.
05:49 Mira: yes, if you tag requests at the SDK layer with feature flags, the console will attribute costs accordingly. we've seen teams use this for product analytics.
05:56 Erin: relevance to Optimize: are there recommendations for quantization or batching that change per-token cost in the console?
06:02 Mira: yes Optimize suggestions appear as cost-savings cards. they will estimate token latency/cost delta if you switch quantization or batching. the console then simulates projected monthly savings if applied.
06:15 Lisa: nice. will those suggested savings be realistic? we've been burned by aggressive estimates from other vendors.
06:20 Mira: the estimator uses past latency, batch patterns, and the model profile; it's conservative by default. we include confidence bands in the recommendation.
06:30 Alex: i want to show a quick hands-on scenario — suppose payments team runs two routes: payments-sync and payments-batch. payments-batch is cheaper per token but uses more total tokens. we'll show how billing splits.
06:43 [demo: toggles to route comparison view]
06:50 Mira: here is the 'Route Comparison' view — charts compare token volume, normalized cost, infra percent, and top models. you can select both routes and then 'allocate costs by usage' or 'allocate reserved share'.
07:07 Lisa: i like the chart showing 'cost per thousand tokens' — it's easy for execs. can we export charts for reports?
07:12 Mira: yes PNG export plus a PDF 'route summary' for a given month.
07:18 Erin: ok show me the raw CSV output — want to see exact fields.
07:21 Mira: pasting snippet: 2027-08-15T03:00Z,payments-batch,team=payments,152000,120000,32000,gpt-small,0.0009,5.12,1.6,us-west-2
07:36 Tom: that 'reserved_alloc' value — is that dollars or percent?
07:40 Mira: dollars. it's the amortized share of reserved infra allocated to that route for the time window.
07:46 Lisa: do you keep historical baseline snapshots? if someone changes mapping later will exports change retroactively?
07:52 Mira: snapshots are stored per-billing-cycle. mapping changes are not retroactive; we snapshot the mapping so previous months remain consistent.
08:01 Erin: that helps.
08:03 Alex: ok quick pause — any burning compliance questions?
08:06 Jamal: confirm SAML/SSO and RBAC — we need fine-grained RBAC so finance only sees aggregated exports and not user prompts.
08:12 Mira: yes RBAC supports route-level permissions and an 'exports viewer' role that only sees aggregated cost artifacts, not request details.
08:19 Jamal: good. also want to verify retention windows — for audit we need 2 years of aggregated metrics.
08:24 Alex: retention is configurable up to 36 months for enterprise customers.
08:28 Tom: what about data residency? we need EU for EU customers.
08:32 Mira: region selection and residency are available for Hosted, and Private lets you fully control region.
08:38 Erin: ok good. back to chargeback model — how would you recommend we start the pilot? what minimal set of routes/tags?
08:45 Alex: start with 3 routes: payments-batch, payments-sync, and risk-scorer. have FinOps owners for each, run a 14-day baseline on Hosted or Dedicated canary, then reconcile with billing. we typically run a 2-week synthetic baseline + one real week production mirror.
09:00 Lisa: what's the expected delta between console numbers and our cloud bill?
09:05 Mira: typically cloud infra charges and token costs diverge because cloud bills include GPU amortized differently; our console's 'infra-only' should align within 3-7% if Dedicated pool pricing is used. if you compare to raw cloud VMs there may be more variance.
09:19 Erin: ok that seems acceptable.
09:22 Alex: i'm going to show how to set up a 'chargeback rule' quickly.
09:27 [screen: Rules builder]
09:31 Mira: rules are declarative — you can define conditions (route == payments-batch AND team_tag == payments) then set allocation method: 'per-token' or 'reserved-split'. you can also set manual overrides.
09:44 Lisa: can rules be audited? we need an audit trail for any manual adjustments.
09:48 Mira: yes all rule changes are versioned and appear in the audit log with actor and timestamp.
09:55 Tom: is there an API to query historical allocations? we have internal dashboards that pull everything.
09:59 Ravi: yep, the Console has a REST export API and a streaming webhook. you can pull allocations per-month via API.
10:10 Erin: any pitfalls you've seen when teams first adopt this for chargeback?
10:14 Alex: common ones: incomplete tagging, trying to attribute very low volume routes which creates noise, and expecting per-token parity with cloud bills. we help with a 'tag completeness' audit and a small script to backfill tags for a POC window.
10:27 Lisa: I'll want that tag completeness report.
10:29 Alex: noted — Mira will run a tag completeness check during the baseline.
10:33 [customer cross-talk planning schedule]
10:41 Alex: ok time check — 10 minutes left, can we walk through a sample invoice view?
10:46 Mira: yes switching to 'Invoice Preview' — this is how chargeback rows appear: route, owner, token_count, cost, markup, total_allocated. you can group by team or product and download GL-ready CSV.
10:58 Lisa: do you support multi-currency? we invoice teams in local currency.
11:02 Mira: yes conversions at month close based on configured FX rates.
11:08 Erin: for the pilot we'd like Hosted first, then move to Dedicated if numbers look good — is that path supported?
11:13 Alex: absolutely. we recommend Hosted quickstart to validate tagging and rules, then Dedicated for steady-state capacity if you want lower unit cost and isolation.
11:20 Tom: last infra question — do you support k8s-based private runtime or only on VMs?
11:26 Mira: Private can run in your k8s or on VMs; we've done both. the console integrates with either.
11:31 Alex: quick recap and next steps?
11:33 Erin: yes pls.
11:34 Alex: action items: send playbook and sample export (Alex), Mira runs 24h synthetic baseline and tag completeness (Mira), customer to provide route-to-owner mapping and decide Hosted vs Dedicated pilot (Erin/Tom). we'll target pilot kickoff week of 2027-09-13.
11:49 Lisa: sounds good. add security docs to the folder too.
11:52 Alex: will do. thanks everyone.
11:55 Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcript contained minor word swaps (e.g., 'K V cache' vs KV cache) and occasional speaker mislabels; cleaned lightly but kept conversational artifacts.
